messages:
maya: seeing a sudden spike of 503s from hosted inference for model 'vega-13b'. root cause looks like upstream worker died mid-request (customer-reported). I captured a few logs from the node. paging @oncall_sre :eyes:

samir: got it. what do logs show? any OOM or segfault?

maya: snippet from host logs: ```Mar 17 09:12:03 inferd[1245]: runtime: caught signal SIGABRT
Mar 17 09:12:03 inferd[1245]: fatal error: abort signal received
Mar 17 09:12:03 inferd[1245]: backtrace (most recent call first): ...
Mar 17 09:12:03 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 1245 (inferred-runner) total-vm: 32000000kB````

julian: that looks like an OOM kernel kill (OOM-killer). Is this GPU memory or host memory?

maya: kernel OOM points to host RAM, but downstream logs show the model service printed `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` then `segfault` almost immediately. sequence: high mem + then cuda failure + abrupt exit.

oncall_sre: I'm on it. Can you share model/instance details? which flavor and batch config?

maya: vega-13b-quant, node `hosted-vega-12`, gpu A100 40GB, batch-size autoscale enabled, burst qps ~450 at the time. model context ~32k tokens for one customer.

samir: large context plus batching could push both GPU and host memory. suspect our prefetch/batching concat path allocated huge host buffer. did we recently ship any prefetch change? @deploy-bot show last prod patch for infer-runtime.

deploy-bot: release 2026.03.12-infer-prefetch-optimizations deployed to prod 2026-03-12 03:20 UTC to subset of hosts.

support_sean: this customer (acct: ACCT-9982) hit timeouts and raised a support ticket. they're seeing ~25% of requests 503 for last 45m. they're on a critical run. any quick mitigation?

oncall_sre: mitigation plan: 1) disable autoscaling batching for that model (reduce memory spikes) 2) route traffic for that account to dedicated fallback pool (smaller contexts) 3) cordon the affected host to avoid noisy neighbor restarts. I'll run step 1 now.

julian: also recommend temp pin to a lower-context model variant (vega-13b-compact) while we triage. 32k context on 40GB A100 is risky with concurrent batches.

maya: step 1 applied: batching autoscale turned off for vega-13b in region eu-west-1 for that account. immediate drop in 503s from 24% -> 6% over ~2m. still seeing a single host crash earlier though.

samir: capturing coredump and GPU debug: can someone upload /var/crash/inferd_1245/core and `nvidia-smi -q` output before it reaped? we need to know if GPU driver reset happened.

maya: uploading to #infra-uploads/3114002000. `nvidia-smi` on next host shows no persistent ECC errors, but driver logs show: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, Ch:000, PID:1245, GPU has fallen off the bus`.

oncall_sre: "GPU fallen off the bus" + kernel OOM + cuda error implies interplay between host OOM and GPU driver instability. hypothesis: prefetch change allocated large pinned host buffers that blew past host memory, driver dropped GPU, process segfaulted.

julian: agree. next steps: rollback prefetch change for the runtime variant on affected hosts, add a host memory guard for prefetch (cap pinned allocation), and add autoscaler safety for extreme context sizes.

support_sean: told customer we have mitigation and routing in place and are continuing investigation. they asked for ETA to full fix.

oncall_sre: ETA: rollback to be staged to subset tonight (2h), full rollback + fix + gating tomorrow morning. I'll open a postmortem ticket and link here. tagging @samir for follow-up on gated rollout.

maya: creating incident ticket INC-20260317-311400 with notes and uploads. thanks team. :thumbsup:

samir: reassigning to eng-runtime to implement pinned allocation cap. I'll also add alert rule for host memory pressure during high-context requests.

julian: leaving a note to product: recommend discouraging >16k contexts on vega-13b hosted until we have memory guards in.

support_sean: customer emailed to say service improved after routing change. will keep monitoring and update when they confirm stability.

maya: closing the immediate customer escalation — will keep thread for postmortem updates.
